title: WhatsApp Group Chat: Participant limit increases to 1,500 members
summary: WhatsApp increases group chat participant limit to 1500 members
detailed: WhatsApp, the popular messaging app, has increased the limit on the number of members that can participate in a group chat from 1,024 to 1,500, according to information from WABetaInfo.

This significant increase allows group chat administrators to add 476 additional people to a single conversation, which is expected to make communication easier for large organizations, schools, and clubs.
The previous increase in the group size limit from 512 to 1,024 members was made in November 2022, alongside the global rollout of Communities and the ability to poll within conversations.
The ability to host up to 1,500 members in a group chat is an important step in this direction, offering new opportunities for collaboration and real-time information exchange.

This significant increase allows group chat administrators to add 476 additional people to a single conversation, which is expected to make communication easier for large organizations, schools, and clubs.
This change is especially important for organizations that rely on direct and mass communication.
Until now, many teams were forced to separate their members into different conversations, which often led to confusion and loss of information.
With the new limit, organizations can keep all their members in a single conversation, making it easier to share information and organize activities.
This increase requires no action from users to activate.
Existing groups will get the additional capacity automatically as the change is pushed to their accounts.
This means users don’t have to worry about complicated activation processes or upgrades.
They just need to keep their app updated to the latest version to benefit from the new increased limit.

This feature also applies to individual group conversations within WhatsApp Communities, which bring together related groups under a common hub.
Communities is a feature that allows multiple group conversations to be brought together under a common umbrella, making it easier to organize and manage large groups.
WhatsApp hasn't officially announced the change, and the app's Help Center still lists the maximum group size as 1,024 members.
However, the new feature has already started rolling out to some users using the latest versions of WhatsApp for iOS and Android.
This suggests that the company is testing the new feature on select users before rolling it out more widely.
The previous increase in the group size limit from 512 to 1,024 members was made in November 2022, alongside the global rollout of Communities and the ability to poll within conversations.
These changes enhanced the WhatsApp experience, making it even more attractive for large groups who want to keep their communication in a single environment.
This new feature is expected to further enhance the WhatsApp.
Users who wish to benefit from the new increased limit do not need to do anything more than keep their app updated to the latest version.
